categories.main_business_segments: eBay operates a single reportable business segment: its global Marketplace platforms, which include the online marketplace at www.ebay.com, localized counterparts, and a suite of mobile apps. The company connects millions of buyers and sellers worldwide, facilitating the exchange of goods and services in a wide range of categories.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: eBay's core technologies include proprietary user interfaces, transaction processing, database and network applications, and APIs for third-party developers. The company leverages artificial intelligence, computer vision, and data analytics to personalize experiences, enhance search and discovery, and streamline listing and payment processes. Its infrastructure is built on industry-standard architectures for scalability and reliability.
categories.primary_customers_markets: eBay primarily serves individual consumers (C2C) and business sellers (B2C) who list and sell goods on its platform, as well as buyers seeking value and unique selection. Major end markets include parts & accessories, consumer electronics, home & garden, collectibles, and luxury goods. The platform attracts both casual sellers and professional merchants.
categories.geographic_coverage: eBay operates in more than 190 markets globally, with significant operations in the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, and Australia. In 2021, approximately 54% of Gross Merchandise Volume (GMV) was generated outside the U.S., reflecting a strong international presence.
categories.supply_chain_position: eBay acts as a third-party online marketplace, operating downstream in the supply chain by connecting buyers and sellers but not holding inventory or directly handling logistics for most transactions. It facilitates payments, listings, and advertising, serving as an intermediary platform.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: eBay's strategic focus is on enhancing the marketplace experience through technology, driving GMV growth, increasing revenue via managed payments and advertising, and maintaining healthy operating margins. R&D priorities include building compelling category experiences, expanding managed payments, developing seller tools, and leveraging AI for personalization and trust-building features like authentication and buyer protection.
categories.revenue_model: eBay generates revenue primarily through transaction fees (take rate) on successful sales, payment processing fees, and first-party advertising (Promoted Listings). Additional revenue comes from store subscriptions, listing fees, and marketing services. The majority of revenue is tied to the value of transactions completed on the platform.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: eBay faces intense competition from global and local online marketplaces, retailers, and specialized platforms, including Amazon, Alibaba, Walmart, Etsy, Facebook, Google, and others. eBay differentiates itself with a focus on unique and value-oriented inventory, but competes on price, selection, trust, and user experience. Many competitors have larger customer bases or broader service offerings.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2021, eBay enabled $87 billion in GMV and generated $10.4 billion in net revenues, representing 17% year-over-year revenue growth. The company had 147 million active buyers and 17 million sellers, with approximately 1.5 billion live listings. eBay maintains strong cash flow and profitability, though GMV was flat year-over-year as pandemic-driven growth normalized.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: eBay emphasizes a unique value proposition of connecting buyers and sellers globally with a broad, relevant, and often unique inventory, including pre-owned and refurbished goods. The platform offers low barriers to entry for sellers, robust buyer protection, authentication for luxury goods, and data-driven tools to optimize sales, positioning itself as a trusted, inclusive, and sustainable commerce leader.
